newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Former Czech opposition MP joins ruling party.
newsitem.headline: Former Czech opposition MP joins ruling party.

text.p: Tomas Teplik, a former parliamentary deputy of the Czech opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD), has joined Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS), an official in ODS's parliamentary office told Reuters.

"I can confirm that the (ODS parliamentary) caucus voted to accept Teplik," Vlasta Kloncarova of the ODS parliament office said. The switch gives the ruling coalition 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house of parliament, after having a minority since last June's general elections.

Another former CSSD member, budget committee chairman Josef Wagner, declared himself an independent last weekend after the Social Democrats expelled him for voting with the centre-right three-party coalition last December on the 1997 budget.
The coalition can now claim it has enough votes to block any attempt by the opposition to dissolve the cabinet. Wagner has said that he would remain "an independent Social Democrat".
He said that he would not necessarily vote with the government to give the coalition an absolute majority.

Klaus's coalition, which has held power longer than any conservative government in post-Communist Europe, lost a large majority in parliament last June, after a surprisingly strong second place showing by the centre-left Social Democrats.
